$schema-note: The fixed Event Runner admin identity (design brief §5.2; admin story docs/plans/2026-08-27-admin-identity-story.md, amended by docs/plans/2026-09-10-admin-editorial-desk.md). Not a seventh preset: the admin obeys data-mode and ignores data-theme, so the generator emits this set ONCE PER MODE and never once per (theme, mode) pair. That emission rule is the mechanical statement of 'the admin ignores data-theme', and apps/web/src/lib/themeModes.test.js asserts it.
$palette-note: Channels are [r, g, b] numbers, never hex strings. The desk (2026-09-10): a deep rail anchors the tool against a calm cool-grey canvas; white panels sit on that canvas; one action colour carries every primary control, link and focus ring; the state grounds are soft tints that always pair with a word. Both modes are authored value by value. The rail and the action family below are the NAVY FALLBACK: on a deployment they are rewritten per mode from the event's brand colour, or from a house scheme the operator picks (schemes below), by resolveAdminScheme in packages/shared/src/theme.cjs, which derives every step from one seed and holds every pair to its contrast bar.
$palette-words-light: desk-grey canvas, paper-white panel, navy ink, slate secondary, steel data ink, hairline blue-grey rule, action blue, proof amber, checked green, oxide red, night-navy rail
$palette-words-dark: night canvas, lifted charcoal panel, bone ink, dusk secondary, steel data ink, banked rule, lit action blue, held amber, held green, held red, deep-night rail
$colors-note: Every entry resolves under :root[data-mode='light'] and :root[data-mode='dark']. Both values are authored; no dark value is derived from its light twin. Grounds are the surfaces of the desk; inks sit on them; rules structure them; states always pair with a word; the action family is the tool's own blue and never the client's; the rail family is the navigation's dark ground and the inks that read on it.

--admin-ground-rgb.$role: (a1) The canvas. The base page ground behind every panel: a calm cool grey, never pure white.

--admin-ground-raised-rgb.$role: (a2) A panel, the title band, a dialog: the white work surface sitting on the canvas, separated by a hairline rule, never by a shadow.

--admin-ground-soft-rgb.$role: (a3) A muted region inside a panel: a table head, a nested group, a quiet hover.

--admin-ground-proof-rgb.$role: (a4) The draft ground: the tint behind a Draft badge and behind a row with unpublished changes.

--admin-ground-input-rgb.$role: (a5) The ground inside a form control. White in the day, a shade below the panel at night, inside a control rule that clears 3:1.

--admin-ground-alarm-rgb.$role: (a6) The destructive and rejection ground. Low chroma; the words carry the weight.

--admin-ground-ok-rgb.$role: (a7) The ground behind a Live badge and a completed-action notice.

--admin-ground-info-rgb.$role: (a8) The ground behind an informational notice and a neutral badge.

--admin-ink-rgb.$role: (b1) Primary text. Navy near-black in the day, bone at night. Never pure black, never pure white.

--admin-ink-secondary-rgb.$role: (b2) Descriptions, hints and support text. Clears the text bar on every ground it sits on.

--admin-ink-data-rgb.$role: (b3) The mono role's ink for identifiers, paths and counts, tuned so a dense column does not out-weigh the prose beside it.

--admin-ink-inverse-rgb.$role: (b4) Text on a filled control: on the action blue and on the ink.

--admin-ink-disabled-rgb.$role: (b5) Dead matter and disabled controls. Still readable: it holds the text bar on the soft ground too, because the dead badge sets a word in it at the smallest step.

--admin-ink-link-rgb.$role: (b6) The admin's own link colour: a text link, a row action, the ink on the action-soft ground. Never the client accent.

--admin-rule-hairline-rgb.$role: (c1) Row, field-group and panel separators. The workhorse.

--admin-rule-strong-rgb.$role: (c2) A secondary button's boundary and a table-head boundary. Non-text interface, so it clears 3:1 against the canvas.

--admin-rule-control-rgb.$role: (c3) A form control's boundary. Non-text interface under WCAG 1.4.11, so it clears 3:1 against both the input ground and the panel.

--admin-rule-header-rgb.$role: (c4) The rule under the title band. It clears 3:1 against the canvas so the band reads as an edge, not a smudge.

--admin-rule-alarm-rgb.$role: (c5) The rule around a destructive or rejected surface.

--admin-state-live-rgb.$role: (d1) Ink for the published state; its ground is --admin-ground-ok-rgb. Always paired with the word 'Live'.

--admin-state-draft-rgb.$role: (d2) Ink for the unpublished states; its ground is --admin-ground-proof-rgb. Always paired with the word 'Draft' or 'Live with unpublished changes'.

--admin-state-error-rgb.$role: (d3) Ink for a rejection; its ground is --admin-ground-alarm-rgb.

--admin-state-caution-rgb.$role: (d4) Ink for a warning that is not a failure; its ground is --admin-ground-proof-rgb.

--admin-state-ok-rgb.$role: (d5) Ink for a completed action; its ground is --admin-ground-ok-rgb.

--admin-state-info-rgb.$role: (d6) Ink for a neutral fact stated in a badge or a notice; its ground is --admin-ground-info-rgb.

--admin-action-rgb.$role: (e1) The action colour: the filled primary button, the current rail item, the focus ring. Authored here as the navy fallback; a deployment derives it from the event's brand colour or a house scheme.

--admin-action-hover-rgb.$role: (e2) The primary button under the pointer.

--admin-action-soft-rgb.$role: (e4) The soft action ground: a secondary button under the pointer, a selected row, a neutral badge. The link ink reads on it.

--admin-action-soft-hover-rgb.$role: (e5) The soft action ground one step darker.

--admin-focus-ring-rgb.$role: (f1) One visible focus colour on the light surfaces: the action blue, which clears 3:1 on the canvas, the panel and the input ground in both modes. Never the client accent.

--admin-focus-ring-rail-rgb.$role: (f2) The focus colour on the dark rail, where the action blue would sink into the ground.

--admin-rail-ground-rgb.$role: (g1) The navigation rail: the deep ground that anchors the tool against the canvas. Authored here as the navy fallback; a deployment derives it from the same seed as the action colour.

--admin-rail-ground-raised-rgb.$role: (g2) A lifted region on the rail: the job-mark tile's frame, the account foot.

--admin-rail-ground-hover-rgb.$role: (g3) A rail item under the pointer.

--admin-rail-current-rgb.$role: (g4) The current rail item's ground: the action blue, filled, with the rail ink on it.

--admin-rail-ink-rgb.$role: (g5) Text on the rail: the current item and the event name.

--admin-rail-ink-muted-rgb.$role: (g6) Text on the rail at rest: inactive items, group folios, the signed-in address. Clears the text bar on every rail ground.

--admin-rail-rule-rgb.$role: (g7) The rules on the rail: under the lockup and above the account foot.

--admin-client-accent-ink-rgb.$role: (h2) The ink that reads on the accent, for the rare case the mark is filled behind a glyph.

$alias-note: (h1) The one client-owned colour, written from config/theme through buildRuntimeThemeCss like any other override. It defaults to the admin ink, so an unset accent renders as a plain ink mark rather than as nothing. The legibility floor lives in packages/shared/src/theme.cjs: the resolved accent is measured against --admin-ground-raised, the title band it sits on; when it fails 3:1 in a mode, the mark falls back to --admin-ink and the editor says so.
$scheme-note: The house schemes an operator may pick instead of the brand colour (desk amendment, part m). Each is ONE seed per mode; resolveAdminScheme derives the whole rail and action family from it exactly as it does from a brand colour, so a house scheme and a brand colour clear the same bars by the same construction. The ids are the words the picker shows; add a scheme by adding a seed.
$component-note: (h3) One client-accent slot: the page-header mark. The client accent appears there and nowhere else, so the rule is greppable; any other reference to --admin-client-accent in apps/web fails review. (g8) The current rail item's leading marker is the rail ink, a structural signal that belongs to the tool, not to the client.
$scalar-note: (c) rules ship as a colour plus a width pair (brief §3.7). (f3) the focus ring is 3px, offset so it never collides with a rule. (i) shape: one control radius, one panel radius, one small radius for a badge; nothing is a pill. (j) the admin type scale is the desk's own six steps, fixed and never writable from config/theme; the tier-2 editorial scale belongs to the paper, not the tool. (k) a control is 2.75rem tall on every pointer; density comes from the gutters, never from the targets.
$font-note: (l1, l2) Source Sans 3 carries everything a person reads as language, across its 400 to 700 weights; IBM Plex Mono carries everything the machine owns. No --admin-font-* token is ever writable from config/theme, so the generator always emits these two faces whatever preset a deployment runs.
